No. 1 of 2024  In  CRA No. 323 of 2024  1 - Krishna Kumar Nagdev S/o Mohanram Nagdev Aged About 26 Years  Resident Of Village- Rajpuri, Police Station-Sitapur, Dist.- Surguja, C.G., Current   Village And Outpost- Latori, Police Station- Jainagar, Dist.- Surajpur, C.G.

---- App  Versus  1 - State Of Chhattisgarh Through Station Officer Jainagar, Dist.- Surajpur, C.G.
 ---- Responden (Cause-title taken from Case Information System) 16/04/2024

This appeal is against the impugned judgment dated 31.01.2024 passed by Additional Sessions Judge (FTC), Special Court, Surajpur,
District Surajpur, CG in Special Case No. 49/2021 convicting the accused/appellant under Sections 363, 366-A, 376 (2)(n) and 506-B of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act and sentencing him to undergo RI for 4 years and fine of Rs. 5000/- u/s 363, RI for 6 years and fine of Rs. 5000/- u/s 366-A, RI for 10 years with fine of Rs. 5000/- u/s 376(2)(n), RI for 2 years with fine of Rs. 5,000/-
u/s 506-B, Life Imprisonment with fine of Rs. 5,000/- u/s 6 of the POCSO Act, plus default stipulation.

entities.text:
Additional Sessions Judge (FTC), Special Court, Surajpur,
District Surajpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Case of the prosecution in brief is that on the date of incident when the prosecutrix had gone to ease herself and did not return, a search was made but she was not found anywhere.
Thereafter she came to know that the accused/appellant had lured her away on the pretext of marriage and committed forcible sexual intercourse for two days by keeping her in village Lalitpur.

Mr. Sajal Kumar Gupta, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the accused/appellant has been implicated in a false case because of a dispute between the appellant and brother of the victim with regard to sale and purchase of paddy.

He submits that prosecutrix was aged about 18 years on the date of incident and therefore, the sentence may be suspended and the accused/appellant be bailed out keeping in mind the fact that the disposal of the appeal is likely to take some more time.

On the other hand, Mr. Shreyansh Agrawal, PL for the State/ respondent opposes the prayer for suspension of sentence and submits that looking to the seriousness of the offence committed by the accused/appellant, the accused/appellant does not deserve the benefit of suspension of sentence Krishna Kumar Nagdev vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81281295/
1 and grant of bail.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents appended with the bail application.

entities.text: Krishna Kumar Nagdev vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, also considering the evidence available on record and the fact that the victim was aged about 18 years at the time of incident and the accused/appellant appears to have been implicated on account of dispute between him and the brother of the victim and the appellant is in jail since 27.06.2021 and further that the hearing of this appeal would take prolonged period of time, we deem it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of the appellant.
Accordingly, the substantive jail sentence awarded to appellant- Krishna Kumar Nagdev by the learned trial Court is hereby suspended.
He shall be released on bail on his executing bail bond with two sureties to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 10.05.2024.

He shall thereafter, appear before the concerned trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to him by the said Court, interval being not less than 06 months, till final disposal of this appeal.
Consequently, I.A. No. 1 of 2024 is allowed.

It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only confined for disposal of aforesaid I.A. filed in this appeal and it shall not be construed as an expression of opinion of this Court on the merits of the matter.
List this matter for final hearing.
C.C. as per rules.
